title: Reference build orders
overview:
## Animals and opening adjustments

Adapt to the food on your map. Animal sets can vary or mix; the build is a guide, not a fixed script.

| Type | Starting food |
|---|---|
| Boar-type hunt | Elephant/rhino: 400 each; boar/tapir: 340; javelina: 300 |
| Herdables | 8 sheep/goats/pigs at 100 each, or 7 cows/buffalo at 150 each |
| Chickens | 6–8 at 75 each; cannot be lured, so a mill is needed for efficient gathering |
| Deer | 2–4 at 140 each; usually push them under the TC |

Adjust boar timing, mill location and berry workers to the animals available and how many deer you push. Keep changes modest while learning a build.

Going up 1–2 population earlier offers pressure at the cost of resources and tighter execution. Going later is more forgiving and leaves more time to wall. Adapt after mistakes or enemy disruption.

builds.notes: Prioritize early Fletching over a second range. Preserve roughly 10–15 archers for Crossbowman + Bodkin Arrow. Against mass skirmishers, add scouts if needed. During the Castle transition, add a range or stable; on arrival, get Bow Saw and choose between extra TCs, monks, Ballistics or siege.

3 villagers on wood. Burgundians: get Double-Bit Axe as soon as the first lumber camp is ready and resources allow; do not wait for the Castle transition.
1 villager lures a boar.
1 villager builds a house, then a mill on berries.
Strongly recommended: push 3 deer under the TC.
Add 3 hunters under the TC and lure the second boar.
Add 4 berry villagers and an extra house.
After boars run out, move sheep villagers onto 3 farms.
Add 5 woodcutters; keep one lumber camp.
2 villagers on gold.
Click Feudal Age; target arrival 11:20.
When food under the TC runs out, remaining villagers chop stragglers.
Build a barracks.
2 villagers build a stable.
Build a Blacksmith with 1 villager.
Add 2 woodcutters; keep one lumber camp.
Click Castle Age; target arrival 14:50.
After clicking Castle Age, train 3–4 Scouts for 4–5 including the starting Scout. Locate relics and watch for forward villagers.
Prioritize Bow Saw; fit Horse Collar and Heavy Plow around military spending. Aim for 8–10 farms and reserve 175 wood for a Monastery.
Immediately build a Monastery and research Light Cavalry. Reserve gold for 2 Monks; keep cavalry and Monks in separate control groups.
Add Husbandry next. If the opponent keeps contesting with Scouts, add Forging and more cavalry. Add cavalry armor as needed later.
Add a third Monk when you control the approaches. Collect on separate routes; aim for most relics, or all five when ahead.
After the Monastery, add TC #2 (275 wood / 100 stone). Around 12–14 farms is a guide; add more if cavalry production continues.
Add TC #3 once relic control is stable; roughly 18–22 farms is a guide. Delay it for needed troops, without waiting for every relic to be returned.
Add TC #4 once villager production is sustainable. Reserve another 100 stone and follow the economy reference toward Imperial Age.

reference_sheets.title: Burgundians · Arena economy
reference_sheets.subtitle: Default: contest relics with Light Cavalry, add TC #2, then expand to 3–4 TCs as control stabilizes. Farm counts are guides.

cards.title: ① Castle transition: cavalry and Monastery
cards.body:
Build a Barracks during the Feudal transition, then a Stable + Blacksmith. Click Castle before training Scouts to 4–5 total. Prioritize Bow Saw; fit in Heavy Plow.
On arrival: Monastery + Light Cavalry, then 2 Monks and Husbandry. Add Forging for sustained cavalry fighting. Add a third Monk when you can protect separate collection routes.

cards.title: ② Expand while contesting relics
cards.body:
Move depleted-food villagers to wood and a second Lumber Camp: roughly 14–18 on wood, 3–5 on gold, the rest on food. Aim for 10–12 farms at Castle; reserve Monastery and upgrade costs.
Add TC #2 around 12–14 farms; TC #3 around 18–22 once control is stable. Continued cavalry production needs more farms and may delay TC #3.
Add TC #4 when relic control and villager production are stable; send 3–4 villagers to collect another 100 stone. Choose the 4-TC Boom reference for the pure-boom alternative.

cards.title: 3 · Wheelbarrow, Hand Cart and mining
cards.body:
Wheelbarrow: around 30–39 villagers after the new TCs finish (105 food / 50 wood); keep the other TCs working.
Hand Cart: check at 50–60 villagers (180 food / 200 wood); avoid delaying villagers, monks or TC #4.
Gold Mining / Stone Mining: 60 food / 75 wood each. Delay for 2–4 short-term miners; consider with 6–8 long-term miners. Do not research Stone Mining just for TC #4's 100 stone.

cards.title: 4 · Imperial around 95 pop
cards.body:
At 75–90 villagers: roughly 20–25 wood / 12–18 gold, rest food with stone as needed. Aim to click Imperial around 95 pop. A university with a monastery/workshop, or a castle, covers the building requirement.
During the transition, use 2–3 woodcutters for 2 workshops. Plan about 4 ranges for Hand Cannoneers and 3 stables for cavalry, building in stages as funds allow. Add barracks for spears; a second blacksmith helps parallel upgrades.

cards.title: 5 · Imperial: Chemistry first
cards.body:
Start Chemistry immediately (300 food / 200 gold, 100 seconds), then 1–2 Bombard Cannons. Pair Hand Cannoneers with some cavalry; against cavalry, start pikes and add Halberdier when affordable.
Upgrade the units you use: archer armor for HC; infantry armor/attack for pikes; Elite Skirmisher, ranged attack and armor for skirms. Stable techs are half price; no Bloodlines.
With a castle, remember Conscription and Burgundian Vineyards; do not click Flemish Revolution casually. Ballistics does not improve HC or trebuchets; no Siege Engineers.

cards.title: 6 · Around 130 villagers
cards.body:
Example: 55 food / 30 wood / 35 gold / 10 stone. For heavy light-cavalry production, use 65–75 food and reduce gold/stone. Reduce stone if no castle is needed.
Short of cannons: add wood/gold. Short of frontline: add food. Use separate control groups and protect/repair your siege.

reference_sheets.title: Burgundians Arena: 4-TC Boom
reference_sheets.subtitle: Alternative: a safe 3-to-4-TC boom. Switch to the defensive reference under pressure.

cards.title: 1 · Castle: three TCs and farms
cards.body:
After sheep/berries, move to wood and a second lumber camp. Aim for 14–18 wood / 2–3 gold, rest food. Around 8–10 farms during the transition; prioritize Bow Saw, then Heavy Plow if it will not delay TCs.
Reserve 550 wood + 200 stone for two TCs, with 4–5 woodcutters building each; budget another 100 wood for the camp. Add farms from 12–14 toward 16–18.

cards.title: 2 · Nearby relics before TC #4
cards.body:
With 3 TCs placed, around 30–35 villagers, optionally add a Monastery and 1 Monk for nearby safe relics; scout the route first.
Send 3–4 villagers to collect another 100 stone. Around 40–50 villagers, once production is sustainable, use 4–5 builders for TC #4 (275 wood). Keep roughly 16–20 on wood and expand toward 24–28 farms, then continue adding farms.

cards.title: 3 · Wheelbarrow, Hand Cart and mining
cards.body:
Wheelbarrow: around 30–39 villagers after the new TCs finish (105 food / 50 wood); keep the other TCs working.
Hand Cart: check at 50–60 villagers (180 food / 200 wood); avoid delaying villagers, monks or TC #4.
Gold Mining / Stone Mining: 60 food / 75 wood each. Delay for 2–4 short-term miners; consider with 6–8 long-term miners. Do not research Stone Mining just for TC #4's 100 stone.

During the transition, use 2–3 woodcutters for 2 workshops. Plan about 4 ranges for Hand Cannoneers and 3 stables for cavalry, building in stages as funds allow. Add barracks for spears; a second blacksmith helps parallel upgrades.

Upgrade the units you use: archer armor for HC; infantry armor/attack for pikes; Elite Skirmisher, ranged attack and armor for skirms. Stable techs are half price; no Bloodlines.
With a castle, remember Conscription and Burgundian Vineyards; do not click Flemish Revolution casually. Ballistics does not improve HC or trebuchets; no Siege Engineers.

cards.body:
Example: 55 food / 30 wood / 35 gold / 10 stone. For heavy light-cavalry production, use 65–75 food and reduce gold/stone. Reduce stone if no castle is needed.
Short of cannons: add wood/gold. Short of frontline: add food. Use separate control groups and protect/repair your siege.

reference_sheets.title: Romans · Feudal
reference_sheets.subtitle: Start MAA with a few skirmishers. Scout before choosing more pressure or Castle Age. Worker and army counts are starting points.

cards.title: 1 · Get the first MAA forward
cards.body:
Train 3 militia during the Feudal transition; move out if the route is safe, then reinforce with 2. Do not let reinforcement costs delay Man-at-Arms.
On reaching Feudal, research Man-at-Arms, then Double-Bit Axe. If resources are tight, upgrade the first 3 before completing the intended 5.

cards.title: 2 · Blacksmith → range
cards.body:
At about 5 farms, build a blacksmith and get Scale Mail Armor. Reserve house wood, then use the next 175 wood for a range.
Start with 2–3 skirmishers to target repair villagers, then Fletching. Add Horse Collar once defense and resources allow.

cards.title: 3 · Respond to immediate pressure
cards.body:
If archers arrive early, prioritize the range. Start with 4–6 skirmishers and scale with enemy numbers; add archer armor when taking fire.
Against scouts, add spears to protect skirmishers. Roman double infantry armor does not apply to skirmishers. Do not sacrifice defense just to save for Castle.

cards.title: 4 · Pressure while walling
cards.body:
MAA force repairs; skirmishers target the repair villagers. Switch to another resource if blocked. Avoid chasing archers or diving TCs.
Small-wall wood/gold, then connect houses to woodlines. Keep the perimeter compact. Reinforce MAA only while they can still achieve value.

cards.title: 5 · Save for Castle
cards.body:
After 5 MAA, keep 2 on gold. If stopping MAA, upgrades are covered and 200 gold is banked, temporarily reduce to 1. Check gold at roughly 400 food.
Reference: 20–24 food / 12–14 wood / 2–4 gold. At 39 villagers: 22 food / 14 wood / 3 gold. Choose allocations that fit your total villager count.

cards.title: 6 · Choose the Castle branch
cards.body:
A Castle click around 38–42 villagers is a reference. Pressure may delay it; do not wait for a villager count if you can safely advance now.
Preserve your army and reserve workshop wood/gold. Choose Archers, Cavalry archers or Knights; use Castle Age for infantry/ram pressure, TC #2 and Imperial preparation.

reference_sheets.title: Romans · Castle Age
reference_sheets.subtitle: Choose the branch matching the main threat: archers/crossbows, cavalry archers, or knights. Counts and timings are references, not deadlines.

cards.title: 1 · 38–45 villagers: prepare the first push
cards.body:
Castle click around 38–42 villagers (roughly 18–20 minutes in a smooth game). Aim for 12–16 wood / 5–7 gold, rest food. At 40: 20 food / 14 wood / 6 gold.
Arrival around 21–23 minutes: Long Swordsman + Chain Mail Armor first for an infantry army, then Squires/attack. Use 1–2 woodcutters for a workshop; under archer pressure do not wait for all upgrades. Save starting stone for TC #2.
New villagers add farms/wood. Small-wall resources and protect any forward workshop without emptying home defense.

cards.title: 2 · 42–55 villagers: rams + TC #2
cards.body:
Start around 8–12 Long Swordsmen + 1–2 rams. Clear escorts, then production/resource access before TCs. Unload infantry when melee units attack the rams.
Once stable, TC #2 can follow around 21–24 minutes in a smooth game: reserve 275 wood / 100 stone, use 4–6 woodcutters, then keep 2–3 on stone.
Reference: 14–18 wood / 6–8 gold / 2–3 stone, rest food. At 50: 23 food / 16 wood / 8 gold / 3 stone. Stop adding rams against mangonels, unbeatable escorts or a blocking castle.

cards.title: 3 · If the push stalls, change composition
cards.body:
Archers: Elite Skirmishers + scorpions. Cavalry archers: same core, earlier Ballistics. Knights: Pikemen + monks.
Against infantry, use Long Swordsmen in front of scorpions; avoid fighting from behind in numbers/upgrades. Eagles can flank the siege.
Against mangonels, spread and retreat scorpions, then add your own mangonel. Infantry can flank siege only through a safe route; otherwise fall back.

cards.title: 4 · 45–65 villagers: prepare a castle
cards.body:
For a timely first castle, increase stone from 2–3 to 6–8 villagers. At 60: 26 food / 18 wood / 9 gold / 7 stone.
Save 650 stone plus walls, repairs and TC #3 reserves. Use 6–8 builders on a safe site covering resources and retreat routes.
After completion, return to 2–3 stone miners; move the rest to food/gold.

cards.title: 5 · 60–85 villagers: TC #3 and Imperial
cards.body:
Once the castle and army are stable, consider TC #3 at 60–80 villagers: 275 wood / 100 stone, 4–6 builders. Delay until after the Imperial click if timing is urgent.
Check Hand Cart at 60–80 villagers; if saving for Imperial, use another TC during the transition. Catch up Wheelbarrow, Bow Saw and Heavy Plow.
Saving for Imperial: 16–20 wood / 12–16 gold / 2–3 stone, rest food. Check at 65–85 villagers and click when affordable and defensible.

cards.title: 6 · Imperial transition
cards.body:
Use 1–2 woodcutters to add barracks/workshops. Reserve trebuchet, main-unit upgrade and reinforcement costs. Add missing TC #3/Hand Cart only after checking military funds.
Upgrade the army you actually have; do not queue every option at once. See Imperial for production, Conscription and siege timing.

reference_sheets.title: Romans · Versus archers
reference_sheets.subtitle: For archer/crossbow armies with minor melee support. Switch pages if cavalry archers or knights become the main threat.

cards.title: 1 · Feudal: early skirmisher support
cards.body:
Get Double-Bit Axe first. At 5 farms build a blacksmith, then reserve house wood and add a range at 175 wood. Against close two-range pressure, build the range earlier.
Keep skirmishers together; check Fletching and archer armor. Add a second range if one cannot keep up. Horse Collar follows once defense allows.

cards.title: 2 · Castle: upgrade and add a workshop
cards.body:
With skirmishers already massed, prioritize Elite Skirmisher + Bodkin Arrow; add armor in stages. Reserve 200 wood and use 1–2 builders for a workshop without waiting for every upgrade.
Start with 2–3 scorpions, then 4–6 if stable. Prioritize units and an answer to enemy mangonels before Ballistics. Bodkin Arrow improves skirmishers, not scorpions.

cards.title: 3 · Enemy mangonels or skirmishers
cards.body:
When a mangonel appears, insert one of your own into workshop production. Spread and retreat scorpions; keep 1–2 villagers repairing safely.
Against many skirmishers, add Long Swordsmen, Chain Mail Armor and Squires. Flank mangonels only with a safe route; do not chase through crossbow fire.

cards.title: 4 · Wall routes, keep an escape
cards.body:
Connect houses to walls and woodlines; check corners for gaps. Small walls stop melee units, not arrows.
Keep gatherers away from exposed walls and leave a path to the TC or rear resources. If builders are already in range, rebuild farther back.

cards.title: 5 · 45–65 villagers: food and wood
cards.body:
Two TCs, 60 villagers: 28 food / 22 wood / 8 gold / 2 stone. A starting allocation for two ranges + one workshop, not guaranteed nonstop production.
Reserve gold for Elite Skirmisher and Bodkin Arrow. Add farms if food is short; move excess gold miners to food/wood. More infantry needs food/gold; mangonels need reserved wood/gold.

cards.title: 6 · Expand once stable
cards.body:
Use 4–6 woodcutters for TC #2 after holding. Against crossbow/mangonel pressure, defense comes first.
Keep 2–3 on stone; increase to 6–8 for a castle. See Castle Age for TC #3, Hand Cart and Imperial preparation.

reference_sheets.title: Romans · Versus cavalry archers
reference_sheets.subtitle: For cavalry archers or Mangudai with a cavalry screen. Prioritize range, Ballistics and holding positions; do not chase.

cards.title: 1 · Two ranges + one workshop
cards.body:
Stop adding Long Swordsmen/rams when cavalry archers become the main threat. Keep existing infantry as escorts. Train skirmishers from two ranges; use 1–2 woodcutters for a workshop.
Start with 2–3 scorpions, then 4–6. Keep Elite Skirmishers with them. Mangudai are especially dangerous to exposed siege.

cards.title: 2 · Elite Skirmisher, Bodkin, Ballistics
cards.body:
Upgrade existing skirmishers with Elite Skirmisher + Bodkin Arrow, then armor in stages. Once the core army and production are stable, build a university for early Ballistics.
Bodkin Arrow does not affect scorpions; Roman scorpions do benefit from Ballistics. Get urgent units first, but do not indefinitely skip upgrades.

cards.title: 3 · Add a screen against cavalry
cards.body:
If cavalry reaches the siege, start with about 4–6 Pikemen and infantry armor; scale with enemy numbers. Keep them beside skirmishers and siege rather than chasing.
Add 1–2 monks against knights. Open the Versus knights guide if cavalry becomes the main threat. Against mangonels, add your own rather than only more scorpions.

cards.title: 4 · Reduce the area to defend
cards.body:
Use houses and short walls between woodlines to close side routes. Add a second inner wall where space allows.
Keep gatherers off the outer wall, preserve retreat paths and check gates/tree-cut gaps. If cavalry archers leave, hold resources; do not chase with slow siege.

cards.title: 5 · 45–65 villagers: transition resources
cards.body:
Two TCs, 60 villagers: 28 food / 22 wood / 8 gold / 2 stone; more wood and less gold than the infantry/ram example.
Reserve resources for Elite Skirmisher, university and Ballistics. Once upgrades are paid, move surplus gold miners to food/wood. More pikes need food; a castle needs extra stone without spending all production wood.

cards.title: 6 · Hold chokepoints and prepare Imperial
cards.body:
Use walls, woods and chokepoints to narrow fights. Check side routes before moving defenders away. Keep 2–3 on stone; use 6–8 for a timely castle.
See Castle Age for TC #3 and Imperial. Heavy Scorpion and Halberdier priorities depend on the enemy screen; see Imperial.

reference_sheets.title: Romans · Versus knights
reference_sheets.subtitle: For knights or other melee cavalry as the main threat. Spears hold entrances; monks stay behind. Do not get pulled away from home.

cards.title: 1 · Stabilize with pikes and monks
cards.body:
Against a few knights, protect resources with existing spears and add 1–2 monks for conversions/healing. Research Pikeman and armor as cavalry numbers grow.
About 6–10 Pikemen is a starting reference, split across entrances. Reaching that count does not automatically make it safe to move out. Avoid chasing cavalry.

cards.title: 2 · Spend Castle wood/gold on defense
cards.body:
Under heavy cavalry pressure, use 1–2 woodcutters for a monastery. Add a second barracks if production cannot keep up. Prioritize Pikeman/armor over extra Long Swordsmen or rams.
Add a workshop for the enemy support: scorpions against ranged units, mangonels against enemy mangonels. Against knights alone, stabilize pikes/monks first.

cards.title: 3 · Close entrances, not just resources
cards.body:
Connect short walls and houses to woods; check corner gaps and leave villager retreat routes toward TCs.
If knights attack a wall, build a house or second layer safely behind it and hold the breach with pikes. Avoid opening gates for enemy cavalry; watch tree-cut gaps and flanks.

cards.title: 4 · Respond to ranged support
cards.body:
Against archers/skirmishers supporting knights, add scorpions and keep existing Elite Skirmishers. Answer enemy mangonels rather than blindly massing siege.
Do not chase with all pikes and monks. Protect monks and resources. If ranged units become the main threat, switch branches and retain a small anti-cavalry screen.

cards.title: 5 · 45–65 villagers: sustain TCs and pikes
cards.body:
Two TCs, 60 villagers: 32 food / 18 wood / 8 gold / 2 stone. A defensive starting point, not a fixed ratio.
Gold first funds monks and upgrades. After adding a workshop, move some food villagers to wood and add gold if needed. Build TC #2 only where its builders can survive.

cards.title: 6 · Expand, mine stone, prepare Imperial
cards.body:
Use 4–6 builders for a safe TC #2 near wood/gold while leaving pikes/monks home. Keep 2–3 on stone; increase to 6–8 for a castle.
See Castle Age for TC #3, Hand Cart and Imperial. If cavalry remains numerous, remember Halberdier, armor, attack, Conscription and enough barracks.

reference_sheets.title: Romans · Imperial
reference_sheets.subtitle: Upgrade your existing army. Preserve fighting strength and production before optional technologies. Counts are references.

cards.title: 1 · Add production during the transition
cards.body:
Use 1–2 woodcutters for barracks/workshops. If producing infantry and pikes together, start around 3–4 barracks and scale with queues/resources.
Reserve trebuchet, core-upgrade and reinforcement costs. Use another TC for missing Hand Cart without exhausting military funds.

cards.title: 2 · Open the way with trebuchets
cards.body:
Against castles, start with 1 trebuchet and 2–3 woodcutters for safe repairs. Keep the frontline ahead of siege.
Spread and retreat scorpions threatened by mangonels; add a siege answer. Do not rely on infantry chasing enemy siege head-on.

cards.title: 3 · Infantry core: Legionaries and upgrades
cards.body:
Continue the Long Swordsman line into Legionaries and catch up infantry armor/attack. Prioritize this only while infantry remains central.
Add a Centurion when affordable. Choose Ballistas/Comitatenses for the army you are using; do not stop reinforcements just to complete the tech tree.

cards.title: 4 · Cavalry threat: halbs + barracks
cards.body:
Against a heavy cavalry screen, research Halberdier and check infantry armor. Legionaries and halberdiers share barracks; upgrades alone do not provide production.
Remember Conscription, but fund survival units and the first trebuchet first. With few enemy cavalry, a small screen may suffice.

cards.title: 5 · Scorpion core: Heavy Scorpion + Ballistas
cards.body:
Prioritize Heavy Scorpion when scorpions are your core. At roughly 8–10 with continued production, consider Ballistas. Do not miss Ballistics against cavalry archers.
Romans lack Bracer, so Elite Skirmishers are support later on. Use Heavy Scorpions behind a frontline and keep their control group separate.

cards.title: 6 · Rebalance and resume growth
cards.body:
Adjust after each reinforcement cycle: siege needs wood/gold, infantry needs food/gold. Avoid following one fixed ratio forever.
Keep 2–3 stone miners for repairs and the next castle. Resume villagers once stable; add a missing third TC if military funds allow.

reference_sheets.title: Burgundians · Defending a castle drop
reference_sheets.subtitle: Move exposed gatherers, seal breaches and counter follow-up units. Resume growth when safe, then prepare Imperial. A counter-castle or TC pause is not automatic.

cards.title: 1 · 28–40 villagers: relocate and wall
cards.body:
Check Loom. Move exposed wood/gold/stone workers to safe alternatives and add camps. If no safe mine exists, prioritize defense and use the market for shortfalls.
Use 2–3 woodcutters for short inner walls beyond castle range, joining houses and thick woods. Check corners, ends and tree gaps; lock unused gates. Leave a second rear seal against petards.
Delay TC #3 if defense needs the resources. Existing TCs need not all stop; if on one TC, add a safe second after essential defense.

cards.title: 2 · 35–50 villagers: castle only if needed
cards.body:
Counter-castle if core resources cannot be held with units/walls. A peripheral enemy castle may not need one. Urgent allocation: 10–14 wood / 4–6 gold / 8–10 stone, rest food, without starving defense.
Stone needed = 650 + unpaid walls + repair reserve − stockpile. With 100 left after TC #2, mine 550 plus reserves. Use 6–8 safe builders; cover access/resources and leave rear repair space.
Afterward reduce to 0–3 stone. A second castle is situational; avoid endless counter-castles that delay Imperial.

cards.title: 3 · 30–45 villagers: the right building
cards.body:
Use 1–2 woodcutters for the workshop or monastery you need; roughly 10–14 wood / 4–6 gold, rest food/stone as needed. Do not automatically build both.
Ranged units/mangonels at walls: start 1 mangonel, add a second if pressure continues, and spread them. Knights/valuable convertible units: 1–2 monks; light cavalry: add spears. Avoid trading siege into high-damage ranged fire.
Defend breaches and follow-up units, not the castle itself. Use melee/siege against rams; Loom villagers only if unescorted.

cards.title: 4 · 30–60 villagers: economy techs in stages
cards.body:
Double-Bit Axe and Horse Collar form the base; prioritize Bow Saw. Heavy Plow must not delay the first mangonel/monks. Existing farms do not receive the full added food.
Wheelbarrow around 30–40 villagers after two-TC production and defense stabilize. Hand Cart around 50–60 if booming longer; delay while saving Imperial.
Gold Mining suits 8–12 long-term miners. Skip Stone Mining for a brief first-castle burst followed by 2–3 miners. Delay later mining/wood/farm techs.

cards.title: 5 · 50–65 villagers: save for Imperial
cards.body:
Two-TC reference: 12–16 wood / 8–12 gold / 0–3 stone, rest food. At 60: 32 food / 14 wood / 12 gold / 2 stone. Save only once gathering and breaches are stable.
Check from about 50 villagers; 55–65 is not a mandatory stop count. Near 1000 food / 800 gold, briefly pause one TC if useful; resume after clicking as military funds allow.
Check prerequisite buildings. During the transition add a university and needed workshops/ranges, reserving Chemistry and first-unit costs.

cards.title: 6 · 60–75 villagers: push back and recover
cards.body:
With a castle, queue a trebuchet on arrival and Chemistry at the university. Without one, hold through Chemistry and cannon production. Do not let castle techs delay the first trebuchet.
Gunpowder reference: 16–20 wood / 14–18 gold / 0–3 stone, rest food; 2–3 safe repair villagers. Protect siege and clear threatening units first.
HC against infantry; pikes against cavalry, Halberdier under heavier pressure. Add appropriate armor. Resume villagers when stable; no need to clear every castle before adding a TC. Build houses!

reference_sheets.title: Arena · Defending a castle drop
reference_sheets.subtitle: Villager ranges assume a typical Fast Castle. React earlier if pressure arrives earlier. Builders come from your existing allocation.

cards.title: 1 · 28–40 villagers: assess the drop
cards.body:
Check builders, escorts and construction progress. Intercept only with enough force and a safe retreat; do not rush your economy into an almost-finished castle.
Use 1–2 villagers for safe camps and move exposed gatherers. A castle that denies no key resources and has no follow-up may require little response.

cards.title: 2 · 28–40 villagers: 2–3 inner wallers
cards.body:
Build short walls beyond castle range, allowing for enemy range upgrades. Connect houses and thick woods; seal side routes and endpoints.
Leave space between outer and inner walls so a breach does not immediately expose your economy. Keep workshops/monasteries behind the line.
Leave a rear second seal against petards and check tree-cut gaps.

cards.title: 3 · 35–50 villagers: a defensive castle
cards.body:
If walls/units hold, do not rush a counter-castle. Otherwise use 8–10 stone miners, about 10–14 wood / 4–6 gold, rest food. Budget castle cost + walls + repairs − stockpile, with civilization discounts.
Use 6–8 builders beyond enemy range, covering the breach and resources. After completion and reserves, reduce to 0–3 stone and return to food/gold.

cards.title: 4 · 30–45 villagers: first defenders
cards.body:
Use 1–2 woodcutters for the most urgent building. Roughly 10–14 wood / 4–6 gold supports initial defense; allocate stone separately.
Ranged pressure: workshop + 1 mangonel, then a second if needed. Knights/valuable units: monastery + 1–2 monks; light cavalry: spears.
Avoid direct siege trades into high-damage ranged units. Counter follow-up armies, not the castle. Stop adding defenders once the threat is contained.

cards.title: 5 · 50–70 villagers: Imperial when stable
cards.body:
Two-TC reference: 12–16 wood / 8–12 gold / 0–3 stone, rest food. Reduce stone if repairs/castles are not needed.
With safe resources and a stable line, pause one TC if needed for 1000 food / 800 gold. Under repeated breaches, fund units first. Counts are not mandatory stop points.
Do not keep booming as if unpressured, or stop all growth just because a castle exists. Check prerequisites and first Imperial army costs.

cards.title: 6 · 60–80 villagers: counterpush
cards.body:
Use 2–3 woodcutters for safe siege repairs. Start around 16–20 wood / 12–18 gold, stone for repairs, rest food; cavalry needs more food.
With a castle, open trebuchets. Cannon civs need a university, Chemistry and unit funds. Protect siege from melee and prioritize enemy siege threats.
Without a castle, survive the Chemistry/production gap. Resume villagers and TCs once stable, even before all enemy castles fall.

reference_sheets.title: Burgundians · Hold Fast Castle vs towers
reference_sheets.subtitle: Flexible starting allocations, not a fixed script. Builders come from existing workers. Keep the Fast Castle only while you can gather safely behind the walls.

cards.title: 1 · To Feudal: relocate and seal gaps
cards.body:
Use 2–3 villagers to connect houses with short walls to thick woods. No need to wrap walls outside every house. Seal corners/ends and leave an inner passage; do not anchor on a lone tree being chopped.
Stone walls require Feudal: use palisades/houses first, then reinforce threatened gaps. If towers already hit the line, rebuild behind it and allow for Fletching range. Move exposed gatherers first.
Check Loom before frontline construction, repairs or fights. It cannot be researched during an age-up. Build houses!

cards.title: 2 · Feudal: Castle click or counter-tower
cards.body:
If walls and gathering are safe, build market + blacksmith inside and save 800 food / 200 gold. If key resources will be denied, counter-tower first. Loom needs another 50 gold.
For more walls/towers, start 3–5 stone miners; briefly use 5–6 for an urgent second tower. Short walls with enough stockpile may need none.
Stone wall: 5 stone per tile; tower: 125 stone + 35 wood. Ten wall tiles + one tower cost 175 stone, before repairs. Do not sell/spend all starting stone.

cards.title: 3 · Counter-tower placement
cards.body:
Cover where enemy villagers would build their next tower. Place behind the inner wall, with safe rear garrison/repair access. Deny expansion and protect essential resources; gold is not always the priority.
Use about 4–6 builders. Do not crowd forward merely to duel an old tower, or sit so far back that new towers are free. Wall the base while retaining access; start 1–2 repairers.
Garrison while enemy villagers build. Teutons can force construction; one tower is not guaranteed to hold. Add firepower or fall back rather than repair forever.

cards.title: 4 · After clicking Castle: 27–32 villagers
cards.body:
Workshop line: 10–12 wood / 4–5 gold / 0–3 stone, rest food. At 30: 12 food / 11 wood / 5 gold / 2 stone. Take builders from wood; reduce stone once covered.
Workshop + first mangonel: 360 wood / 135 gold. A later ram needs 160 wood / 75 gold. Also budget houses, walls and repairs; this need not all be banked on arrival.
Keep existing wood/farm upgrades. Bow Saw only if defense allows; delay Heavy Plow, Wheelbarrow and mining techs. Siege does not benefit from blacksmith armor/attack.

cards.title: 5 · Castle: hold first, then clear towers
cards.body:
Use 2 woodcutters for a safe workshop. Start 1 mangonel + 1–2 repairers to deter forward villagers and breaches. Resume gathering if stable; add a second only for continued pressure.
Mangonel range is 7; a basic tower has 8, more with upgrades. Start at exposed outer towers, repair safely and withdraw damaged siege. Avoid overlapping tower fire.
Add 1 ram only with safe access and escorts. Ram hits tower; mangonel threatens villagers attacking it. Use existing Flemish Militia or 2–3 knights as needed. Towers can target mangonels; avoid friendly fire.

cards.title: 6 · Restore gathering, then TC #2
cards.body:
Around 30–40 villagers with siege production: 12–14 wood / 5–7 gold / 0–3 stone, rest food. Add farms if food is short. Enemy forward villagers lose income, but your relocations/repairs do too; do not assume a lead.
Stabilize on one TC first. Fund another siege unit if it solves active pressure; do not stockpile units forever or clear harmless towers urgently. Reassess if the enemy advances or adds army.
Add a safe TC #2 (275 wood / 100 stone) when you can sustain villagers. No need to clear all towers; no automatic counter-castle or 3–4 TC boom.
